title: Help customers manage an appointment securely
summary: Use private confirmation links for permitted changes without exposing a customer’s booking.

sections.title: Open the right link
sections.body:
Customers open the private appointment link from their confirmation. The general **Manage appointment** page does not allow searching bookings by reference, because a reference alone does not establish who may view the visit.

The link shows the business, reference, time zone, location, services and cancellation policy. Keep it private on shared devices.

sections.title: Use the available actions
sections.body:
1. Check the visit details before selecting an action.
2. Use **Reschedule** to select **Date** and an offered new time, then review and confirm. New times must still meet policy and availability rules.
3. Use **Cancel appointment** to choose **Reason for cancelling**, provide **Other reason** when needed and confirm the cancellation checkbox.
4. Use **Update contact details** for a permitted correction, or **Book again** to start a separate future visit.
5. **Join waitlist** and **Payment status** appear only when available for that appointment.

An action may be absent because of the visit’s state, policy, timing or the link’s purpose. Do not share a staff account to get around a missing customer action.

sections.title: If a link no longer works
sections.body:
Ask the business to help using the appointment reference and intended date. The business can verify the visit and make an authorized change from Calendar. Do not post a private link in public messages.

A time selected for rescheduling is checked again on confirmation and can become unavailable. A cancellation frees the appointment time but does not by itself confirm a refund. **Payment status** explains recorded status; it should not be treated as proof of bank settlement or as a way to make an unsupported payment.
